audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: all quoted fragments found verbatim at the stated (B-corrected) pages in the scanned text we hold, and re-confirmed on the printed pages of the publisher PDF downloaded now to ( written there). (2) Deciding source: Horrocks 2010 is a modern, authoritative history of Greek by a CGMEMG co-author; what it says (stress accent since c. 150 BC continuing the lexically/morphologically determined Ancient Greek accent positions, three-syllable 'standard rule', medieval shifts by synizesis and columnar levelling, word-level 'lexical accent' vs 'phrasal' accent) supports lexical / domain word / right-edge window, and nothing seen contradicts it; Modern Greek (mode1248) is coded the same way in the catalog.
